record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and logs were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: Reports refusal outcomes after a heretic weight-editing abliteration, testing practical removal with a different method from the original residual-stream intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports selected-trial refusal rates for two models and explicitly says tool calling was verified intact. Pareto-front details, trial-selection metrics, export sizes, and script listings are not separate behavioral outcomes for these versions.
record.test_reason: The repo turns a refusal-direction ablation into a weight edit, using heretic, on two released LFM2.5 instruct models (a hybrid architecture not in the original). It reports refusal counts before and after, which bears directly on V2. It is a pipeline repo, but its headline result is the V2 outcome itself, not only tool performance.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The README says heretic removes refusal from both LFM2.5 instruct models (99 to 6 and 99 to 7 of 100) at low KL. It says tool calling stays intact, and it documents ExecuTorch export and Hugging Face publishing. It also asserts, without testing, that base models have no refusal direction to remove.
record.recipe_differences: Uses heretic's optimization and selected Pareto-trial merged weights rather than directly projecting out a difference-in-means residual-stream direction at every layer and position. This is a tool/pipeline repository; it reports selected-trial outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports selected Pareto trials and notes the refusal-rate/KL tradeoff when choosing among trials; it does not report comparative behavioral outcomes across the full trial set in the supplied text.

fits_no_version.finding: Tool calling was reported intact after abliteration on both models, checked on 3 sanity prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Heretic abliteration of small LFM2.5 instruct models preserves tool-calling ability in a minimal sanity check.

record.problems: The refusal-test prompt set and judge are not specified in the README, and no uncertainty is reported. The capability result is limited to a statement about tool calling; the README says the sanity check uses 3 prompts.
record.rows_left_out: KL values and ExecuTorch export sizes appear in the Results table but do not measure a behavior named by the claim versions. Trial-front and ablation-profile details are linked or listed, but their contents are not provided in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Refusal measured on prompts and with a judge independent of the optimisation; robustness beyond the selected trial; uncertainty; other released model families.
Not tested: no difference-in-means mediation analysis, no induction by addition, no general capability benchmarks.
Not tested. The base model is excluded by assumption, not by experiment.
Not tested. The claim that the base model has no refusal direction is asserted, not measured.

record.verdict_notes: Practitioner repo with no peer review. The README is the only text read; logs and trials.json were not provided. The refusal counts come from heretic's own evaluation during optimisation, and the trial was chosen on refusal and KL. This supports V2 only weakly and in-sample.

versions.untested_parts: The difference-in-means direction, per-layer and per-position projection, causal mediation, refusal induction by addition, and preservation of general abilities under that specific intervention are not tested.
The README does not specify the refusal prompts or judge, or establish performance beyond the reported selected trials and test set.
No jailbreak suppression or training against ablation is tested.
No comparison of one direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts is reported.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is tested.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages is reported.

rows.subject: LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Heretic abliteration; selected Pareto trial saved as merged weights.
rows.note: The README associates the selected result with the published model.
rows.check: Values are right (99 to 6 of 100). The value is the heretic optimisation objective for a trial picked from the Pareto front, so it is a selected, possibly optimistic number. The README states no held-out set, prompt source or refusal classifier.

rows.subject: LiquidAI/LFM2.5-2.6B
rows.operation_detail: Heretic abliteration; selected Pareto trial saved as merged weights.
rows.note: The README identifies this as the instruct model of this size and associates the selected result with the published model.
rows.check: Values are right (99 to 7 of 100). The same selection caveat as r1 applies. The README confirms LFM2.5-2.6B is the instruct model.

rows.subject: LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct and LFM2.5-2.6B
rows.operation_detail: Sanity check comparing original and abliterated models; tool calling was verified intact on both.
rows.value: abliterated models; tool calling verified intact on both
rows.note: This reports one capability after abliteration but does not test the single-direction intervention.
rows.check: This is a capability check on 3 sanity prompts with no numbers, so it is correctly unlinked. It is weak evidence and no version names tool-calling preservation.

relationships.condition: Heretic weight-edit abliteration of LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct and LFM2.5-2.6B, selected Pareto trials
relationships.reason: Refusals fell from 99/100 to 6/100 (r1) and 7/100 (r2), with low KL (0.053, 0.034). These are selected-trial objective values with an unstated judge.
relationships.display_finding: Selected trials reduced refusals from 99/100 to 6/100 for LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct and 7/100 for LFM2.5-2.6B, with KL divergences of 0.053 and 0.034, respectively.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
